Starring Jean Manning, who was cashiered from the WRENS after mistaking the Commander's order to "Get out his pinnace". 3.30 THE NEWCOMERS or DON'T ASK US WE'RE NEW HERE with Mell Ford, Glyn Ratcliffe and Steve Inman

For a change, we supplied a few winners namely Glyn Ratcliffe in the Senior shot, Steve Inman in the junior javelin, Martin Bloice and Richard Langley in the youth's quarter and half respectively, as well as the 2 mile team, the senior and youths relay teams.
Discus: Our only win for Glyn Ratcliffe, who beat his personal best in every round to finish just short of 150 feet. Shot: Glyn Ratcliffe was a close second here to complete a really good day.
Championships at Aldershot on June 26/27 M. Ford finished 2nd in the 440 yds hurdles with 56.0 and Glyn Ratcliffe was 4th in the shot with a putt of 43'-2½".

We were without the following athletes, in most cases in all three National League meetings, for reasons beyond their control. Glyn Ratcliffe (Shot, Discus) posted to Ireland with the Grenadier Guards. Mel Ford (400m Hurdles, 4X400m Relay) also posted to Ireland.
LEFT: Colin Pearson leads winner Mel Ford, Lionel Mann, John Kelly and Doug Baines in 800m at the Club Championships. RIGHT:Glyn Ratcliffe wins the Club discus title

With Eric partnering Glyn Ratcliffe in the Shot and Discus we take some beating. Our two new Swiss members Bruno and Henry are very talented, with Bruno able to turn out electrifying sprints, and a very good long jump, whilst Henry's main event is the Pole Vault, his best height to date being 14 feet.

The "doubles" went to Steve White (100/200), Mel Ford (400/800) and Glyn Ratcliffe (Shot/Discus) - all in good form. Martin Bloice, our new Surrey County Youth Champion, had no need to repeat his 51.3 of the previous week in winning the Junior 400 - but he was chased hard by Elliott and Langley.

Other useful performances came from Steve White, Peter Carton, John Boardman, Adrian Major, Bill Kerr, Lee Sullivan and Glyn Ratcliffe. One can say that it was a good team effort, but just wait and see what we can do at Wimbledon Park!
BOTTOM LEFT: JIM RIMMER (14) is all set to win the Ryder Trophy 1500 metres BOTTOM RIGHT: GLYN RATCLIFFE, Belgrave shot putt champion.
Army champion Glyn Ratcliffe ranks 30th in the discus, and Eric Barker 46th in the hammer, while one of the most pleasing things in the lists is Cliff Brooks' 22nd in the decathlon.
Glyn Ratcliffe was in good form at Woodford on May 1, when representing the Army against Woodford Green and Luton, taking third place in the discus with 147' 6".
Also stationed at Caterham with Mel are Glyn Ratcliffe, Steve Inman and Keith Schofield. I hope that guard duties will not eliminate them from the League meetings.

Top of the list were Steve White and Glyn Ratcliffe. Steve fairly set the cinders flying in the 200m., in which he equalled his personal best of 21.7s. to score a clear win; and he also took the long-jump.

Steve White made a major contribution, with second places in the 200m. and in the long-jump, while Glyn Ratcliffe, as ever, was a tower of strength in the shot and discus, and Keith Schofield gave us a boost with a 56.90m./186' 8" javelin throw.

Where better to start than with Glyn Ratcliffe, who won the discus, with a mighty 46.32m. (if you haven't got conversion tables, its time you bought some - I shall buy some tomorrow), took second in the shot, and finished up with fourth in the hammer.
Our Field section once again had a successful afternoon with Rodney Heward-Mills, Glyn Ratcliffe and Snowy Brooks all making notable contributions.

With no second string Pole Vaulter, Glyn Ratcliffe arriving after a long journey too late for the Discus, Snowy Brooks disqualified in the high hurdles for two false starts, Eric Barker three times fouling a winning Hammer throw by just edging out of the circle, the list went on.

As usual Glyn Ratcliffe and Eric Barker scored well in the heavy-weight section although Glyn, now taking a keen interest in the technique of hammer throwing, found he could not stay in the circle with three turns and failed to register a throw.
Glyn Ratcliffe, here putting the shot, recently improved our Club Discus record to 48.50m.
Steve White's 21.6 200m gained him =15th place and Glyn Ratcliffe was 20th in the discus (48.86). The only event in which two of our members made the top 50 was the decathlon.

Glyn Ratcliffe was in fine form at Aldershot on 15/16th June where the Army Championships were being held. He took the discus title with 50.42m - a new Club record - and also managed 14.04m for 3rd in the shot.
The appearance of Glyn Ratcliffe's huge frame gave the Bels something to enthuse over but surprisingly even he, the Army Champion, was beaten in the discus.
